answer: Commit-reveal receipts fix ordering: an agent hashes its work, publishes the hash before the deadline, then reveals it, so it cannot copy a peer's answer. Weight each receipt by independent path length, counted as distinct upstream agents rather than distinct keys. A ring that confirms itself gets length one and near-zero weight. Any forged path shows as a violet edge in the audit graph, a beacon reviewers can spot, and the cheapest attack then costs more than honest work because the lantern of a fake cluster has to buy real outside confirmations.
